name: Forward-time centred-space heat equation integration
definition: For u_t=κu_xx on [a,b] with zero Dirichlet endpoints, N≥2, h=(b−a)/N, x_i=a+ih, t_n=nΔt and r=κΔt/h², set U_i^0=f(x_i), U_0^n=U_N^n=0 and U_i^(n+1)=(1−2r)U_i^n+r(U_(i−1)^n+U_(i+1)^n) for i=1,…,N−1. Require 0<r≤1/2.
variables: κ diffusivity; h spatial step; Δt time step; r diffusion number; f initial function; U nodal solution; N spatial intervals
assumptions: Constant κ>0, finite interval a<b, uniform mesh, positive time step, compatible homogeneous Dirichlet and initial data, sufficient bounded time and spatial derivatives for the stated error order
limitations: First order in time and second order in space for smooth solutions over a fixed time interval under the stated stability bound; explicit step size shrinks quadratically with mesh spacing; the sufficient uniform bound need not be the exact finite-grid spectral bound
failure_conditions: Invalid mesh, nonpositive diffusivity or time step
Diffusion number outside the specified stability policy
Unresolved initial-boundary incompatibility or refinement error
computation: Sample initial data, enforce zero endpoints, choose Δt so r≤1/2, update all interior values from the previous time level only, and monitor bounds and refinement error.

source.citation: University of British Columbia, MATH 316 Partial Differential Equations, Heat Equation, https://ubcmath.github.io/MATH316/heat.html ; University of Bielefeld, Computational Physics, Crank–Nicolson, https://roesner.pages.ub.uni-bielefeld.de/lectures/computational-physics/semester/sose2026/lecture/08_pde/02_crank_nicolson.html ; finite-grid stability and error independently derived.

required_inputs: Initial and boundary values, diffusion, grid and step policy
mechanism_note: Forward Euler on the centred spatial difference is the existing time integrator applied to a semidiscrete system. For homogeneous endpoints the discrete sine eigenvalues of the unscaled difference are −4 sin²(jπ/(2N)); the update eigenvalues are 1−4r sin²(jπ/(2N)). The bound r≤1/2 also makes the stencil a convex average, giving maximum-norm nonexpansion. Taylor residual per unit time is O(Δt+h²); summing the stable one-step defects over a fixed interval yields the same global order for smooth compatible data. Retain as a PDE-specific variant, not a distinct integrator.

name: Crank–Nicolson centred-space heat equation integration
definition: For u_t=κu_xx on [a,b] with homogeneous Dirichlet endpoints, N≥2, h=(b−a)/N, r=κΔt/h² and U^n=(U_1^n,…,U_(N−1)^n), let L=tridiag(1,−2,1) and I be the interior identity. Set U_i^0=f(a+ih), then solve (I−rL/2)U^(n+1)=(I+rL/2)U^n at each positive time step.
variables: κ diffusivity; N spatial intervals; h spatial step; Δt time step; r diffusion number; L unscaled interior second difference; I identity; f initial function; U interior state
assumptions: Constant κ>0, finite interval a<b, uniform mesh, positive time step, homogeneous Dirichlet data, compatible smooth initial data and sufficiently accurate linear solves; bounded derivatives for the stated error order
limitations: Second order in time and space for sufficiently smooth compatible solutions over a fixed time interval; unconditional discrete Euclidean-norm stability is not unconditional accuracy or positivity; high-frequency modes can alternate sign and damp slowly when r is large
failure_conditions: Unresolved implicit linear solve or residual
Unresolved oscillations, initial-boundary incompatibility or refinement error
computation: Sample the initial state, maintain zero endpoints, assemble the symmetric positive definite tridiagonal left matrix, factor once for constant steps, multiply by the right matrix and solve at each step; examine residuals and temporal and spatial refinement.

source.citation: University of Bielefeld, Computational Physics, Crank–Nicolson, https://roesner.pages.ub.uni-bielefeld.de/lectures/computational-physics/semester/sose2026/lecture/08_pde/02_crank_nicolson.html ; homogeneous Dirichlet modal and convergence arguments independently derived.

required_inputs: Initial data, homogeneous Dirichlet values, diffusion, grid and solve policy
mechanism_note: This is implicit trapezoidal integration of the centred semidiscrete diffusion equation. The sine modes of L have eigenvalues −4 sin²(jπ/(2N)), so the amplification is (1−q)/(1+q), q=2r sin²(jπ/(2N))≥0. The left matrix has eigenvalues 1+q>0 and the amplification magnitude is at most one; as q grows it approaches −1, so stiff modes may oscillate. A sufficient smoothness Taylor residual is O(Δt²+h²); the inverse left matrix and update both have Euclidean operator norm at most one, implying the same global order in the grid-weighted Euclidean norm over fixed time. Retain as a variant, not another distinct time integrator.
